Rollcage assessment tool — User manual

Updated November 6, 2026. Open the tool at rollcage-app.vercel.app.

A pre-screening tool, not a certification. The Rollcage assessment tool helps you check a cage against the rules before inspection; a scrutineer still inspects the car and issues its logbook.

Introduction

The Rollcage assessment tool by Frog Racing lets you describe a roll cage once — its design, tubing, installation, welds and seats — and builds a live 3D model of it, rates it with the Frog Safety score, and checks it against the rules of your sanctioning body (ARA, NASA Rally Sport, CARS and others).

It is a pre-screening tool, not a certification: a scrutineer still inspects the car and issues the logbook. Use it to plan a build, check a kit before you buy it, or prepare for a logbook inspection.

What you need: a recent desktop or tablet browser (Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox). There is no account and nothing to install. Your work is stored in your browser on this device only — read Saving, exporting and importing before you put real work into it.

First visit: a short guided tour opens the first time you use the tool in a browser. It shows the tool on a copy of the FIA Article 253 cage template; when the tour ends, that copy is closed (unless you saved it) and you're back in the Rollcage library to pick a cage. You can replay it any time with How it works at the top right; User manual opens this manual. The YouTube logo next to them plays the Rollcage assessment tool tutorial video.

The screen at a glance

At the very top, the YouTube logo plays the Rollcage assessment tool tutorial video, How it works replays the guided tour and User manual opens this manual. Below them, the top of the screen stays in view while you scroll: the rollcage's name, the part selector and the 3D model.

  1. Rollcage name — type a name; it's the name the rollcage is saved under in the library.
  2. Unsaved changes — appears as soon as anything changed since the last save. Click it to open the library, where Save is.
  3. Rollcage library — your saved rollcages, the templates, and Save, Save as, PDF report, Export and 3D print (see The Rollcage library).
  4. 3D Model — shows or hides the model. On a wide screen the model is always shown, so the button isn't there.
  5. Part selector — the eight parts of the assessment, in order. Pick one to work on it.
  6. 3D model — drag to turn it, scroll or pinch to zoom. Reset returns to the default view, Ghost bars shows the bars you could add in grey, Occupants shows the driver and codriver, and Snapshot downloads a picture of the view as it is now. Click a bar to jump to its question, or double-click it to cycle through its designs (a gusset: none, taco, single plate).
  7. Frog Safety score — the cage's safety rating, updated as you answer (green when positive, red when negative). Part 8 explains how it's made.
  8. Compliance — next to the score, how far the cage meets the sanctioning body picked in Part 7, as a percentage (green when it meets the requirements, orange while items still need an answer, red when it fails). Click it to go to Part 7, or click the Frog Safety score to go to Part 8.
  9. Update from pictures — in red next to them while Part 1's pictures disagree with your design. Click it to go to the list of differences.
  10. Picture button (bottom right) — opens the rollcage pictures from Part 1.

Wide screens. When the window is at least 1400 pixels wide, it splits in two: the parts on the left and, on the right, the 3D model with Part 7 or Part 8 below it. The right side stays in place while you scroll the left one, and Part 7 or 8 scrolls on its own. Click the compliance badge or the Frog Safety score on the model to choose which part shows there. While you work on Part 7 on the left, Part 8 shows on the right, and the other way round.

Cards and colours. Each question is a card. A green bar on its left means it's answered and passes, red means it fails, and yellow means it still needs an answer or a check. Answered cards fold up to one line showing the answer; click a card to open it, and Collapse to fold it again.

The Rollcage library

The library is where every rollcage starts and where you save it. It opens by itself on your first visit; after that, open it with Rollcage library at the top right. Back to editing (or Close) returns to the rollcage you were working on. The YouTube logo next to it plays the FIA Article 253 Rollcages Tutorial video, on how roll cages are designed and built.

At the top:

  • Start a new rollcage — a blank rollcage.
  • Import a rollcage from file — opens a .json file exported from this tool or from the Digital logbooks app.

The library has up to five sections, each in its own colour:

SectionWhat it holds
Currently editingThe rollcage open right now, with Save, Save as, PDF report, Export to file and 3D print. Shown once you've started or opened one.
Saved rollcagesEverything you've saved in this browser. A search box filters them once you have several.
Design templatesGeneric designs: a rollbar/half rollcage, a full FIA Article 253 cage, a basic road racing cage, an NHRA drag racing cage, and a Worst cage that shows every warning the tool can give.
Rollcage kitsCommercial kits (Broken Motorsports, Custom Cages, CageKits, AutoPower) with the vendor's diagrams or photos. Not all of them are good cages: the AutoPower rally cage scores well below zero. View product page opens the vendor's site.
Real world cage samplesReal cars, with their photos and tags. Some have a walk-around video (Watch video).

Each card shows a snapshot of the 3D model, the car's photo or the kit's product page, and its Frog Safety score in the top left corner (green when positive, red when negative), with the body it's measured against under it (FIA, NHRA, NASA...).

Click a card to see what you can do with it. On a template, kit or sample, Start from template opens a copy as a new, unsaved rollcage — the template itself never changes. Its pictures and tags come with it.

On one of your saved rollcages the buttons are Load, PDF report, Export to file, 3D print and Delete (see Saving, exporting and importing).

If the rollcage you're editing has unsaved changes when you load or start another one, the tool asks first: Save, Discard or Cancel.

Part 1

Vehicle & pictures

Part 1 records the car and documents its cage with photos. Nothing here is judged against the rules, but the photos are what a scrutineer will compare your answers with.

Vehicle description

Manufacturer, model, year, VIN and weight (kg or lb), plus the drive configuration and the occupants. Left- or right-hand drive mirrors the driver in the 3D model; the weight decides the tubing size some sanctioning bodies require.

Pictures

  • Video overview — a link to a YouTube video of the cage, played inside the tool (Watch video, Change video, Remove).
  • AI processing (beta) — three ways to let the tool do the sorting and tagging:
    • Video walk-around — record a slow walk-around of the car and cage with Add a video: on a phone, record one or choose one from your videos; on a laptop, record with the Laptop camera, choose a file, or Use my phone to record it on your phone. The tool pulls the clear frames out of it: mark one 3/4 front and one 3/4 rear frame as the vehicle pictures; the frames you keep become rollcage pictures. It preselects about one frame per 5 seconds of video (12 for a one-minute walk-around), which you can change. The video itself never leaves your device.
    • Bulk upload with automatic AI sorting — upload up to 20 photos at once; each waits there until the tool places it in a rollcage pictures category (or you move it).
    • AI analysis — tags several pictures at once. AI analysis (beta) opens a window to pick them: the pictures with no element tagged yet start selected, Select all and Select none change that, and Analyze N pictures analyzes them one after the other, as each card's own AI analysis does.
  • Vehicle pictures — one 3/4 front and one 3/4 rear photo of the car. The front one appears on the library card and both go in the PDF report.
  • Rollcage pictures — photos of the cage, sorted into categories. Use Add photos on a category to add photos to it.

Adding photos. Every photo button (Add photos, Add a photo) opens a chooser:

  • On a phone — Take a photo with the camera, or Choose from my photos.
  • On a laptop — Use my phone shows a QR code: scan it, take the photos on your phone and they appear here (this needs an internet connection). Laptop camera takes them with a webcam or USB camera, and Choose a file picks photos already on the computer.
CategoryPhotos
Overview / whole-cage5
Main rollbar (diagonal, harness bar)3
Backstay diagonals3
Roof bars3
Door bars — Left3
Door bars — Right3
Optional bars and gussets (dash bar, harness bar...)8
Mounting feet (one per foot)6

Tagging a picture

Each photo is a small card. The blue number in its corner is how many cage elements it's tagged with; hover it to see the tagged parts. Click the photo to open the card:

  • Edit rollcage elements — turn the 3D model to match the photo, click each bar, gusset or foot you can see, and choose its design. Parts you tagged by hand show in green; AI tags show in magenta, paler the less confident the AI was, and each tag in the list has a dot of its color. Remove all AI tags drops every AI tag of the photo at once, keeping yours. On a wide screen the photo fills the space above the model, and a click anywhere else makes Done flash. Done saves the tags and a Selected parts snapshot of the model.
  • AI analysis (beta) — suggests the tags this photo shows (needs an internet connection). Its tags are marked AI with how confident it was (AI · high, medium or low); they change your design only when you apply them in Differences between pictures and current design.
  • Move to… — moves the photo to another category.
  • Delete photo — asks for confirmation; it can't be undone.
  • ▴ Less folds the card again; clicking an opened photo shows it full screen.

At the bottom of Part 1, two checks compare the photos with the design: Current design elements not documented in pictures lists the bars and gussets no photo shows yet, and Differences between pictures and current design lists tags that disagree with your answers in Parts 2–6.

In Differences between pictures and current design, each row shows what the pictures identify next to your current design, which is picked to start with (picked sides are yellow). Click the other side to switch, or the picked side again to leave the row for later. Select all from pictures and Select all from current design pick a whole side; Apply selected then updates the design from the pictures' side and the pictures' tags from the design's side. A gusset your design doesn't have yet is applied together with the bar design that brings it in. While differences remain, a red Update from pictures badge on the 3D model jumps to this list.

Part 2

Rollcage design (bars & gussets)

Part 2 describes which bars, feet and gussets the cage has. Every choice redraws the 3D model at once, so start here when you design a cage.

Open a card to see the choices, each with a picture of that design taken from the 3D model: a 253-3 base structure as ghost bars and the design's own bars in their 3D model colour (door bars yellow, main rollbar diagonals pink, roof bars orange...), seen from the angle that shows them best, so a card is easy to match with the model. None present shows the ghost bars only. The FIA drawing number (253-x) is in the label.

X designs. An X built from 1 continuous bar and 2 half bars (253-7, 253-12, 253-19, 253-21 and 253-9 door bars) comes as X-configuration 1 and X-configuration 2 (for door bars, config 1 and config 2), one for each tube that can be the continuous one. In the pictures and in the 3D model, the continuous bar keeps its colour and the 2 half bars are drawn white and green, so you can see at a glance which tube runs through. For door bars, config 1 is the continuous bar starting at the bottom front, on both sides.

GroupQuestions
Base structure layout253-1, 253-2 or 253-3 (FIA base layouts), a rollbar (half rollcage) or a custom design; the main rollbar diagonals (253-7); backstays and their diagonals (253-20 to 253-22)
Other structural elementsRoof bars (253-12 to 253-14), roof corner gussets, left and right door bars (253-9 to 253-11, with an optional sill bar; 253-9 is either an X — 1 continuous bar + 2 half bars — or 2 continuous bars with 1 bend or with 2 bends, each with its own icon), windscreen pillar reinforcement (253-15, which can differ left and right: one continuous bar on one side, two bars on the other)
Optional barsHarness bar (253-26/27, 253-28/66), lower main hoop bar (253-30), rear lateral (253-17) and transversal (253-18) reinforcements, rear lower X (253-19), dash bar (253-29), temple bars and windshield reinforcement (253-31), anti-intrusion bars (253-25). Each is picked with picture buttons, its bar or None present.
Mounting feetThe plate design of each foot (253-50 to 253-57), and whether it's bolted or welded
GussetsWhich junctions have a gusset, built as a taco (wrapped sleeve) or a single plate; 253-9's 2 bend bars take one gusset per side, with straight or curved edges. 253-19's rear lower X can have up to 4 gussets (a left/right or a front/rear pair); they're optional, so none costs nothing. The 3D model draws each gusset from the tubes it joins, following whichever door bar crosses the 253-15: a taco as wide as the tubes, flush with them, with a hole in its middle; a single plate thinner

Only the questions that apply are shown: a half rollcage, for example, hides the roof and door bars. Clicking a bar in the 3D model jumps to its card.

Base structure layout. 253-1, 253-2 and 253-3 are grouped under FIA base layouts, then Rollbar (half rollcage / rollbar only) and Other design (Custom design). Each choice shows its own description. Backstays present is only asked for a custom design: every other layout always has its 2 backstays.

Roof corner gussets starts folded, even before it's answered. Its picture shows a 253-3 as ghost bars with all 4 roof corner gussets. All no answers every corner No in one click.

Door bars. Each side's door bar card has two groups that fold open with a click, Designs with sill bar and Designs without sill bar, then None present. The group holding your answer starts open. Picking a design answers the sill bar at the same time, so it's never left unanswered; 253-11 and NASCAR door bars have their own sill bar. No sill bar is a full answer: the card shows the safety risk and the Frog Safety score counts it, but the compliance check doesn't treat it as unanswered. A design with a sill bar ends its label with + sill bar. Once a design is picked, the others are grayed out (they come back on hover), and only the group holding the answer keeps its colour: green with a sill bar, red without.

Gusset locations. In the Gusset design table, and in the gusset tables of Part 4 (dimensions) and Part 5 (welds), each location shows two small pictures of your own cage next to its name: the area around the gusset, with the gusset circled, and a close-up of it. They show the 253-3 structure as ghost bars, the bars the gusset joins in their colours and the gusset in blue, seen from the side of the cage it's on. They follow your design and are redrawn when it changes. Click any of these small pictures (here, and the junction and weld ones in Parts 4 and 5) to see it big.

Part 3

Tubing sizes & materials

Part 3 records what the cage is made of and how big each piece is. These are the measurements a scrutineer checks with a caliper and a tape.

  • Primary tubing — the material, outside diameter and wall thickness of the main structure: main rollbar, laterals, transverse members, backstays and the main rollbar diagonals. Usually 1.75".
  • Secondary tubing — the same for the other bars: roof bars, door bars, sill bars, A-pillar reinforcement, harness bar and the optional bars. Usually 1.5".
  • Tube specifications — says, bar by bar, whether each one uses the primary or the secondary spec. Clicking a bar in the 3D model jumps to its row. The Frog Safety score reads it (see Part 8). Under ARA, at least one continuous door bar on each side must use the primary tubing (1.75" x 0.095"): half bars at that size don't count, and that side's continuous bar row fails otherwise.
  • Mounting feet material and thickness, and Mounting plate size for each foot.
  • Gusset material and thickness — one material for all gussets.

Each card enters inches or millimetres; the minimum sizes come from the sanctioning body picked in Part 7.

Part 4

Installation constraints (angles, distances...)

Part 4 checks how the cage sits in the car: clearances, angles, bends, how close each bar meets its junction and, at the end, the size of each gusset. Angles you enter here also tilt the 3D model, and gusset sizes resize the gussets drawn in it.

GroupWhat you measure
Installation constraintsThe cage stays within the suspension mounting points; the door and windscreen clearances A, B, C, E, H, R1 and R2 (FIA drawings 253-48 and 253-49); the 253-15 dimension A, straightness and bend angle
Main rollbarLeaning angle, tube axis in one plane, number of bends, bend radius and stretch, construction quality
BackstayAngle from vertical
Front rollbarAngle and bends; front feet forward of the foremost rollbar
Bar junction distancesHow far each bar meets its junction, in mm
253-9 bend barsWhere each bend sits (Zone A: at least 300 mm behind the front lateral and 200 mm ahead of the main rollbar) and whether the 2 bars are at most D apart
GussetsFor each gusset: length (E), corner cut-out radius (R < 1.5 D) and hole diameter (H < D). For the 253-9 bend bars' gusset: Lb, Lb', La and W, and Lc for curved edges (at most 0.125 L), illustrated with the FIA drawings. D comes from Part 3.

Two shortcuts save measuring every number: tables with many dimensions have a tick box to confirm them all compliant at once, and junction tables have one for all confirmed within 100 mm. In the 3D model, junctions within 100 mm show green, those over 100 mm show red and are drawn moved along the bar by the distance you entered, and those not measured yet show as ghosts.

At the top of the 253-15, a negative distance means the bar meets the roof behind the transverse member. Its size is what's judged (−150 mm fails like 150 mm), and past −100 mm the bar is drawn back along the side of the roof.

Gussets in the 3D model. Each gusset is drawn at the length you entered: red when one of its dimensions is too short or too long, green once its lengths are all entered and within limits, and a ghost until then (or while Part 3 doesn't give its tube diameter yet).

What to measure. Each row of the bar junction distance tables shows a close-up of your cage: the bar end to measure in green, the bar it's measured from in red, everything else as ghost bars. The gusset tables show where each gusset is (see Part 2).

253-9 bend bars. The bend positions card asks first, per side, for W (the front lateral to the main rollbar) and the gap between the 2 bars, then where each bar bends. With 1 bend per bar, W is the 2 distances added up: enter any 2 of the 3 and the third is filled in (a value you type is never overwritten). The upper and lower bars must bend at the same places (their angles may differ), and the front and rear distances can't add up to more than W. The 3D model draws each bend where you put it, as a share of W, and colours the bend bars red when a bend is outside Zone A, the 2 bars don't match or the gap between them is more than D, green once everything passes. W is copied into the bend gusset's dimensions. Each side shows D, the bigger of the 2 bars' diameters; when D isn't known yet, the gap and gusset rows say they can't be checked until the tube size is entered in Part 3, with a link there.

Part 5

Welds

Part 5 records, joint by joint, whether each weld is complete, including each gusset's. A cage must be welded all the way round every joint.

Each weld row shows a close-up of your cage at that weld: the bar welded in green, what it's welded to in red, everything else as ghost bars. At an X's crossing, only the half bar being welded is green and the continuous bar red. For a foot welded to the chassis, every plate of the foot is green.

  • Weld tables — one per group of joints, matching your design: transverse members, mounting feet, tube-to-foot, laterals and backstays to the main rollbar, diagonals, roof bars, sill bars, door bars, 253-15 supports and each optional bar. Mark each weld Yes (complete) or No.
  • In the 3D model — double-click near a weld point of a highlighted bar (or a foot) to cycle it: green = complete, red = incomplete, ghost = not checked yet. A bar with several weld points is split into colours along its length, in the same order as its table rows.
  • Gusset welds — whether each gusset is welded along its full length. Its dimensions are measured in Part 4.

Your weld answers also answer some sanctioning bodies' grandfathered checks for you, such as No bolt-together cage (Part 7).

Part 6

Seats, belts & routing

Part 6 covers the occupant equipment that attaches to the cage and the body: seat mounts, harness anchors and the lines that run through the cockpit.

  • Seat mounting points — the driver's and codriver's seat mount type (stock mounts, or an FIA chassis-shell or crossmember mount with its plate sizes), and each seat's angle and location.
  • Belt anchoring points — where each shoulder, lap and anti-submarine strap is anchored (harness bar, stock point, plate…), and how many points the belts have.
  • Belt anchor distances and angles — the shoulder-strap distance and angles (FIA 253-61c and 253-61d), the lap belt angle and the 6-point spacing.
  • Routing of lines — fuel, brake and electrical lines kept clear of the cage and protected.

The codriver rows only appear when Part 1 says Driver + Codriver.

Part 7

Sanctioning body compliance

Part 7 checks everything you answered against one sanctioning body's rules and gives a verdict. Pick the body you race with; your answers are kept when you switch, so you can compare bodies. A new rollcage starts with FIA Appendix J Article 253 (generic).

  • Sanctioning body — grouped in the list:
    • No sanctioning body: nothing is judged; only the Frog Safety score rates the design.
    • FIA Appendix J Article 253 (generic) (the default), on its own: the full FIA 253 checklist, item by item.
    • Rally: NASA Rally Sport, American Rally Association and the Canadian Association of Rallysport (CRC), each with its own full checklist, then rally events with rollover protection rules only (see below).
    • Documentation only: bodies with no automatic check yet.
    • Rollover protection rules (from PassTech), in each discipline's group (road racing, HPDE / track day, autocross, hillclimb, drag racing...): only their rollover protection rule is checked — full cage, tubing size for the car's weight, welded plates — and the rest, such as when a roll bar is needed (convertibles...), is listed for you to check by hand. Some ask for your class.
  • Rules to check against — for bodies with grandfathering rules: New construction (a logbook issued now) or Existing logbook (the older rules for cages logbooked before a cut-off date). Many grandfathered items answer themselves from your design — for example the structure, welds, mounting feet, gussets, apertures and tubing; they show From the rollcage design with links to the answers they come from.
  • Verdict — MEETS REQUIREMENTS (green), INCOMPLETE — needs verification (yellow) or NOT COMPLIANT (red), with the count of required items satisfied. The same result shows as a percentage on the compliance badge at the top of the 3D model. Lists of failing and unanswered items follow; click one to jump to it. A cage with backstays but no backstay diagonals picked has none on the model, so they count as None present and fail where the rules require them.
  • Construction route — FIA/ASN homologated (an exact, unmodified match to its homologation papers, exempt from the rest of the checklist) or FIA 253 Ch.8 custom build. A homologated cage can carry photos of its homologation papers.

Hide details folds Part 7 to its verdict and score.

Part 8

Frog Safety score

The Frog Safety score rates how protective the design is, measured against a sanctioning body's rules. It's the number in the top left corner of the 3D model and on every library card; Part 8 shows how it adds up.

  • What it's measured against depends on the sanctioning body picked in Part 7, and the top of Part 8 says which. With no body, FIA or a rally body's full checklist, the design is measured against FIA Article 253's guidelines. A body whose rollover rules come from PassTech (road racing, drag racing, HPDE...) is measured by its own rules instead: FIA's design guidelines still show, in orange, but cost no points, while what that body requires (a full cage, welded plates, its tubing sizes) does. Construction (welds, measurements, junction distances, missing feet) counts whatever the body. So the same roll bar scores +55 for an HPDE but about −195 against FIA, which counts the front structure, roof and door bars it doesn't have.
  • Each line is one design choice, with its answer and its points. Stronger designs earn more: a full 253-3 structure earns +20, an X main rollbar diagonal +10, each door bar design and foot design +5.
  • Tubing stronger than required earns more too. Primary and secondary tubing each get +5 for a diameter at least 3 mm (1/8") larger, and +5 for a wall at least 0.5 mm (0.02") thicker, than the minimum: the sanctioning body's tubing sizes from Part 7 (for a body with rollover protection rules only, the sizes for the car's weight and the tube's material), else FIA Article 253's. Each bar allowed secondary tubing (roof, door, harness, A-pillar bars...) whose tube meets the primary minimum earns +1, up to +10; the score reads the tube sizes, so a cage built from one size everywhere counts too. Tubing under the minimum is a violation (−100). So is a main rollbar marked secondary in Tube specifications.
  • Unsafe choices cost points and show in red with an explanation — for example a missing foot or a bar meeting its junction too far away. A 253-13 roof bar leaves a front roof corner unsupported (−50); with no backstay diagonals bracing the main rollbar, or 253-22's (made for 253-14), it's also a violation (−100). Backstay diagonals left unanswered count as none there. A cage can score below zero: the Worst cage template shows every warning.
  • The links at the top (drive configuration, occupants) take you to the Part 1 answers that change the score. Click any line to jump to its question.

The score only counts what you've answered, so it changes as you fill Parts 2–6.

Saving, exporting and importing

The tool does not save on its own. Your changes live only in the open page until you click Save in the Rollcage library — close the tab or the browser before that and they're gone. Whenever Unsaved changes shows next to the name, save. Reloading or closing the page with unsaved changes asks you first.

Where your rollcages are kept

Saved rollcages and their photos stay in this browser, on this device — nothing is sent to a server. So:

  • Another browser, another computer or a phone won't see them. Use Export to file to move one.
  • Clearing the browser's history or site data deletes them, and a private or incognito window forgets them when it closes.
  • Export the rollcages you care about from time to time: the file is your backup.

Save and Save as

  1. Click Unsaved changes (or Rollcage library) at the top.
  2. In Currently editing, click Save. It turns to Saved ✓, and the rollcage appears in Saved rollcages with a fresh 3D snapshot.
  3. To keep the original and save your changes under another name, click Save as…, type the new name and click Save.

Your saved rollcages

Click a saved card for its actions:

ButtonWhat it does
LoadOpens it for editing (asks first if the open one has unsaved changes).
PDF reportMakes the report of it as last saved.
Export to fileDownloads it as last saved.
3D printDownloads it as last saved, as a model to 3D print (see 3D print below).
DeleteRemoves it and its photos from this browser, after a confirmation. It can't be undone — export it first if in doubt.

Export to a file

Export to file downloads a .json file named after the rollcage (for example RS4 Rally car -- Froooog.json) into your Downloads folder. It holds everything: the answers, the tags, the vehicle and rollcage photos and the event log. Use it to back up, to move a rollcage to another browser or computer, or to send it to someone else.

  • From Currently editing, the file includes any unsaved changes.
  • From a saved card, it's the rollcage as last saved.

The file is plain text but large when it carries photos (several MB). Keep it as it is: don't edit it by hand.

Import a file

  1. Open the Rollcage library and click Import a rollcage from file.
  2. Pick a .json file exported from this tool — or from the Digital logbooks app, which uses the same format.
  3. It's added to Saved rollcages as a new entry, with its photos, and selected; click Load to open it.

An import never replaces an existing rollcage, even one with the same name. If the file's sanctioning body isn't offered here, it's set to none and a message says so.

PDF report

PDF report (in Currently editing, or on a saved card) builds a Rollcage Assessment Report and downloads it: the vehicle and its photos, the 3D model from several angles, every answer part by part, the Part 7 verdict, the rollcage pictures with their tags and the Frog Safety score. It's the document to send to a builder or a scrutineer. The first report needs an internet connection to load the PDF maker.

3D print

3D print (on a saved card, or in Currently editing) downloads a model of the cage to 3D print: a .3mf file for Bambu Studio, PrusaSlicer, OrcaSlicer or Cura. From a saved card it's the rollcage as last saved; from Currently editing, it's the rollcage as it is now, unsaved changes included.

  • The cage is one object, with each bar, foot and gusset as a separate part, named with its FIA drawing number where it has one. Each part keeps its colour from the 3D model; in Bambu Studio each colour becomes a filament. Ghost bars are left out.
  • Include the occupants adds the driver (and the codriver) in their seats. They print inside the cage, so they need supports and can't be taken out afterwards.
  • Scale — from 1:5 to 1:25 (1:10 to start). The dialog shows the printed size and how thick a 45 mm tube prints, and warns when the model won't fit a 256 mm build plate.
  • The feet stand on the build plate; the roof and door bars need supports.
  • Bambu Studio may warn that the file's settings aren't its own and load the geometry only. That's expected: the model, its part names and colours load fine.

Tips and troubleshooting

  • Start from the closest template. A kit or sample with the same layout fills most of Parts 2–6; change what differs, then Save as your own name.
  • Work in order. Part 2 decides which questions the later parts ask, so answer it first.
  • Use the 3D model as an index. Click a bar to jump to its question in the part you're on.
  • My rollcages are gone. They're kept per browser: check you're in the same browser and profile, not a private window. If the browser's data was cleared, import your last exported file.
  • The model or a picture looks blank. Turn 3D Model off and on, or reload the page (Ctrl+F5) — save first.
  • Something doesn't match my rulebook. The rules are encoded from each body's published documents, and the note at the bottom of the page says what each one covers. The scrutineer's call is final; tell Frog Racing at info@frogracing.us.
